svg.title: How a security report is handled
svg.desc: A vulnerability is reported privately through the GitHub Security tab, or by email to admin at brockcsc dot ca. A co-president triages it within days rather than hours. The fix lands on main, which is the only supported line. The v1 tag is then moved onto the fixed commit so callers pinned to v1 pick it up, and a GitHub advisory is published with credit. Two panels list what is worth reporting in this repository — secret leakage into logs, outputs or images, environment blocks escaping their Stack, input handling that crosses between callers, and malicious dependencies — and what is not, including Komodo itself, a caller's own hard-coded secrets, and the fact that the actions need an API key at all.
svg.text: KOMODO-DEPLOY · SECURITY
From a private report to a moved tag
Volunteers, not a security team. No bounty and no SLA — but nothing is left unanswered.
HOW A REPORT TRAVELS
Report it privately
Security tab → Report a vulnerability. The thread stays private until there is a fix, so nothing is published early.
private reporting: enabled
admin@brockcsc.ca if that fails
A co-president reads it
Expect days rather than hours. Nobody is on call, term breaks are real, and the same few people run
everything else in the club — so you get an honest answer, not a fast one.
Fix on main
There is one supported line — whatever v1 currently points at. Nothing is back-ported to older commits,
which is why this file has no version table.
Move the tag, then disclose
v1 is moved onto the fixed commit, so anything pinned to deploy@v1 or ensure-action@v1 picks the fix up on
its next run, with no change on the caller's side. Pinning to a commit SHA instead means updating by hand.
A GitHub advisory follows, crediting you by whatever name you ask for — or by none.
SCOPE — WHAT THIS REPOSITORY IS
WORTH REPORTING HERE
A path where komodo-api-key or -secret can
reach a workflow log, a step output, or the image
Anything that makes the environment block a
caller passes in readable outside its own Stack
Input handling that lets one run touch a Build,
Stack or Action belonging to somebody else
A dependency of the actions turning malicious
NOT IN SCOPE
Komodo itself, and the instance we happen to
run — upstream, and admin@brockcsc.ca
A caller's own workflow hard-coding a secret
instead of passing secrets.KOMODO_API_KEY
That the actions need an API key with deploy
rights at all — that is the whole job
Findings that assume the server is already owned
Code scanning, Dependabot alerts and secret scanning with push protection run on this repository, and main is protected.
Those catch the ordinary things. A human still has to tell us about the rest.
